problem.text:
a. How many ways are there to rearrange the letters of the word SANDWICH?

b. How many ways are there to rearrange the letters of the word SYNONYMS?

steps.title: Where to start: count the letters and look for repeats
steps.body:
Both questions ask how many different orders a word's letters can be put in. If all $n$ letters are different, there are $n!$ orders. If a letter appears $k$ times, swapping those copies among themselves gives the same word, so we divide by $k!$ for each repeated letter:
$$\text{arrangements} = \frac{n!}{(\text{repeats of 1st letter})!\cdot(\text{repeats of 2nd letter})!\cdots}$$

your_turn.prompt: Warm up: how many different arrangements does the word TOOT have?
your_turn.answer: $\frac{4!}{2!\cdot 2!} = \frac{24}{4} = 6$, since T and O each appear twice.

steps.title: Tally the letters of each word
steps.body: SANDWICH has $8$ letters: S, A, N, D, W, I, C, H. They are all different, so nothing needs to be divided out and the count is just $8!$. SYNONYMS also has $8$ letters, but some of them repeat. Careful: check every letter, not just the first repeat you notice.

your_turn.prompt: Which letters of SYNONYMS repeat, and how many times each?
your_turn.answer: S twice, Y twice, N twice; O and M once each ($2+2+2+1+1 = 8$).

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
For SANDWICH: $8! = 40320$. For SYNONYMS we divide by $2!$ three times, once each for S, Y and N:
$$\frac{8!}{2!\cdot 2!\cdot 2!} = \frac{8!}{8} = 7! = 5040$$ The answers are **a) $40320$** and **b) $5040$**.
